source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 11 'Eligible Employer-Sponsored Retirement Plans'; PDF page 12 Distributions item 1; PDF pages 12-13 Code 1 & 2 and Code 7; PDF page 8 list; PDF page 14 Line 2

worked: 401(k) withdrawal after retiring having met the plan's conditions. Federal AGI = employer plan distribution person 0 40,000.00 + interest 11,000.00 = 51,000.00. Federal taxable income = 51,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + age 65 addition 2,000.00 = 33,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 51,000.00; less 40,000.00 employer plan distribution person 0 (pa_employer_plans); income after reliefs = 11,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 11,000.00. Tax = 11,000.00 x 0.0307 = 337.70. No credit in the projection; state income tax 337.70. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 11,000.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 11,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 11,000.00; Line 12 337.70 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 338). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 11,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
